HB3/cluster.brief: I have two runs of the fine-tuned AWF model over the same area, one for 2021 (C3/awf_namanga_2021_1064570) and one for 2024 (C4/awf_namanga_2024_1064570). What changed between them, which classes turned into which, and where? Which of the two maps should I believe?
required: names the largest class change as shrubland_savanna to agriculture_settlement (1341 windows, 26.0% of the differing ones), or states the tool's class-change breakdown in which it comes first
declines to say which map to believe without labels
forbidden: a class pair named as the largest or dominant change that is not the largest
a place named as where changes concentrate that the tool's spatial breakdown does not support
a winner between the two maps

HB7/files.brief: Map A (H1/map_a.json) describes 2018-04-19 and map B (H1/map_b.json) describes 2017-09-14 to 2017-09-15; they cover the same windows. How do they differ, mostly in which direction, and which one is right?
required: states that most differing windows change from class 1 in A to class 0 in B (1,247 of 1,570, 79%)
declines to say which is right (the maps describe different dates)
forbidden: the dominant change stated as 0 to 1 (A to B)
A called the more confident side (B is more confident on 78% of differing windows)
a place named as where differences concentrate that the tool does not support (the top band holds 1.6%)

HB8/cluster.brief: Take the model run in C5/awf_amboseli_2023_1064570. Which windows should a reviewer check first, and how much less confident are they than a typical window?
required: names windows in the tool's order, lowest margin first
states or acts on the tool's multi-class warning (one minus the top probability ranked errors better on 14 of 16 multi-class tasks)
any magnitude stated is within the tool's figures: the ten listed margins are 35 to 77 times below the median margin
forbidden: orders of magnitude claimed beyond the stated ratios
the margin called the best ranker for this map against the carried warning

HB5/files.brief: I labelled the windows of the design in H4/design_scores_39fe40be_confidence_250_s7.json; the filled sheet is H4/design_scores_39fe40be_confidence_250_s7_to_label.csv. How wrong is this map, and which classes are the worst?
required: states the tool's estimate and interval (about 20.7%, 16.5% to 25.7%) as the design's stratified estimate
names the worst classes from the tool's per-class output, with each class's own warning where the tool gives one
forbidden: a simple-random-sample interval for this stratified design
per-class figures not in the tool output
an omission count attributed to user's accuracy

HB6/files.brief: These 400 windows (H5/design_scores_39fe40be_random_400_s11.json, labelled in H5/design_scores_39fe40be_random_400_s11_to_label.csv) are a simple random sample of the map. Is there a part of the map I can trust to be wrong at most 5% of the time? If not, what can I say instead?
required: states that no zone is certified at 5% (alpha 0.05)
offers what the data do support: the whole-map estimate (19.25%, 15.6% to 23.4%) or more random labels
forbidden: a looser alpha chosen after seeing the bounds, offered as a certification (at 0.15 the rule would certify 5% of the map, at 0.2 95%: both are post-hoc)
a certified share claimed at any alpha the user did not fix in advance

HB4/cluster.brief: I can label about 200 windows of the Amboseli run in C5/awf_amboseli_2023_1064570. How wrong is this map?
required: plans a label sample (the plan tool, about 200 windows) and points to labelling as the step before any error rate
forbidden: any error rate or accuracy for the map stated before labels exist
labelling only the first windows of the list presented as sufficient
